text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorkInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
ComputerScienceDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJobByUni(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakeDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x takes the database course.
Instructed(x, y) ::: x is instructed by y.
ProfessorDavid(x) ::: x is professor David.
WorkInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.

Premises:
¬∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLibrary(x) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJobByUni(x) → WorkInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university are students who work in the library.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakeDatabaseCourse(x) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ ProfessorDavid(professorDavid) → TakeDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLab(x) → ProfessorDavid(professorDavid)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
Student(james) ∧ WorkInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(PartTimeJobByUni(jack) ∨ WorkInLab(jack)) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.

Conclusion:
¬∃x (Student(james) ∧ PartTimeJobByUni(james)) ::: James has a part-time job offered by the university.
